obligations.description: rst is an active-high asynchronous reset that clears button sampling history, control state, mode, both timers, and divider remainders; both timer values become zero, and the scan index becomes zero. During reset, LED bits directly driven by switches still follow sw.
obligations.setup: Establish a nonzero time, a nonzero scan index, and button history.
obligations.stimulus: Assert rst during high/low phases and while a button is held, running, and editing; hold for 1/3 edges, then release.
obligations.expected: After reset, the display shows zero and the encoding for index 0, the cursor LEDs are off, and the direction is incrementing; the switch LEDs still reflect the inputs combinationally.
obligations.sampling: Reset takes effect immediately even when asserted between two source clock edges; after deassertion, operation continues according to the input switches and subsequent valid buttons.
obligations.checker: Predict independently from inputs and history, and perform four-state comparisons on native ports; report UVM_ERROR on a mismatch, require a nonzero number of valid comparisons and normal completion.

obligations.description: The four buttons are sampled once every 100000 source clock rising edges; each button must be 1 for 8 consecutive samples to generate one event. Holding a button does not repeat the event; at least one low sample followed by another 8 high samples is required to retrigger.
obligations.setup: Clear history with asynchronous reset, with the controller in stopwatch stopped or clock editing.

obligations.expected: A control/editing effect occurs exactly once, only on the next source edge after qualification is satisfied; short pulses do not change the state.
obligations.sampling: The event goes high after the 8th high sampling edge, and the controller and data editing use that event on the next source edge; buttons are not accepted directly on every source edge.

obligations.description: The initial state enters stopwatch stopped when sw[1]=0; it enters clock running when sw[1]=1 and sw[2]=0, and waits if both are 1. In stopwatch stopped, sw[1] has priority to enter clock mode, followed by R to enter running, then L to enter a single-cycle clear-to-zero state, then D to enter a single-cycle direction-toggle state. Stopwatch running accepts only sw[1] to switch to clock mode or R to stop; L/D have no effect. The clear-to-zero and direction states return to stopped after one cycle.
obligations.setup: After reset, set sw[1]=0 and wait to enter stopped.
obligations.stimulus: Press R to start/stop; while stopped, press L to clear to zero and D to reverse direction; press L/D while running; combine switches and buttons to test priority.
obligations.expected: Predict start/stop, clear, and direction according to the abstract control state; observe through the subsequent time display and cursor LEDs.
obligations.sampling: Control and direction are registered on source rising edges; direction flips on the next edge after the old direction state. All buttons are qualified events.

obligations.description: While the stopwatch is running, one registered tick is generated every 1000000 enabled source edges, and the next source edge advances the time by one hundredth of a second. Time spans 24 hours × 60 minutes × 60 seconds × 100 hundredths of a second, with incrementing carrying through successive fields; in reverse, borrowing propagates from 0 through successive fields to 23:59:59.99. Stopping freezes the divider remainder, and clearing clears the remainder; for each digit, tick takes priority over clear on the same edge.
obligations.setup: Reset to zero; start with valid buttons, and reverse borrowing can establish the boundary from 0 to the end of a full day.
obligations.stimulus: Run incrementally across tick, pause for less than one tick and then resume; clear to zero, reverse direction, and then run to check borrowing and full-day wraparound; run continuously across hundredth-of-a-second and second carries.
obligations.expected: An independent mixed-radix counter updates according to the input enable history, and segment codes are compared within the valid window of each scanned digit.
obligations.sampling: The tick-generation edge and the data-update edge are separated by one source period; after stopping, a tick already generated on the preceding edge can still be consumed.
obligations.checker: Predict independently from inputs and history, and perform four-state comparisons on native ports; report UVM_ERROR on a mismatch, require a nonzero number of valid comparisons and normal completion.

obligations.description: The clock runs autonomously in all non-editing control states, generating a registered tick every 1000000 enabled edges and counting hundredths of a second on the following edge. In W_RUN, sw[1]=0 is handled first to return to stopwatch stopped; otherwise, sw[2]=1 enters editing of the seconds units digit. In an editing state, sw[2]=0 returns to W_RUN; sw[1] does not directly cause an exit during editing. Editing freezes the clock divider remainder.
obligations.setup: After reset, wait for non-editing operation, and set sw[1]=1.
obligations.stimulus: Run the clock across tick, enter editing, wait more than one tick, and then exit; change sw[1] in the editing state, separately combining it with the exit switch.
obligations.expected: Predict using independent clock history and an abstract editing state; time does not advance automatically during editing, and resumes from the remainder after exit.
obligations.sampling: Switches change the control state only on source edges, while the display selection itself follows sw[1] combinationally.

obligations.description: The editing cursor order is seconds units, seconds tens, minutes units, minutes tens, and hours; L moves forward and R backward, with wraparound, and L takes priority over R. U increments the current digit by 1, and D decrements it by 1, with U taking priority over D; seconds/minutes units are modulo 10, tens are modulo 6, and hours are modulo 24, with no carry or borrow between digits during editing. For a digit that actually receives tick, tick takes priority over editing.
obligations.setup: Enter W_SET_S1; traverse the five cursors through valid L/R events.
obligations.stimulus: At each cursor, use D at zero to borrow to that digit's maximum, then U to return to zero; combine movement and editing; apply U/D and L/R simultaneously.
obligations.expected: Predict using an independent decimal digit array, with each digit modulo its own range, and compare against the cursor LEDs and the full scanned display.
obligations.sampling: Qualified button events are applied on source edges; when movement and editing occur on the same edge, editing uses the old cursor.

obligations.description: The display combinationally selects the stopwatch or clock corresponding to sw[1]. The scan index resets to 0, reaches 1 after the first 50000 source edges, and then increments by 1 modulo 8 every 100000 edges. fnd_com follows the sequence 1110/1101/1011/0111 based only on the low 2 bits of the index. Indices 0/1 display hundredths-of-a-second units/tens (sw0=0) or minutes units/tens (sw0=1); 2/3 display seconds units/tens or hours units/tens; 4/5/7 are blank, and 6 displays a dot when hundredths of a second <=50 and is blank when >50.
obligations.setup: Establish a value of 0 after reset, then establish nonzero times, times with different high and low digits, and times on both sides of the dot.
obligations.stimulus: Run naturally through all 8 scan slots; toggle sw0/sw1, check all digits, establish high digits through reverse borrowing; run across 50/51 and observe index 6.
obligations.expected: Determine the scan slot from the absolute count of source edges, predict using decimal decomposition of an independent time value and a segment-code table, and perform four-state comparisons.
obligations.sampling: Changes to the scan index and the selected time take effect combinationally; sample 1ns after source edges, and switch changes between edges can also be observed.
